newsitem.title: USA: SALOMON BROS JULY SALES GROWTH INDEX RISES 6.1 PCT.
newsitem.headline: SALOMON BROS JULY SALES GROWTH INDEX RISES 6.1 PCT.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said Thursday its Same-Store Retail Sales Growth Index rose 6.1 percent in July compared to a 2.3-percent increase in the year-ago period.
It said the index rose 4.6 percent in June 1997.

Salomon Brothers analysts said the index's July gain reflects the effects of more seasonable weather, continued favorable macroeconomic conditions such as high consumer confidence and low joblessness, and relatively easy year-ago comparisons.

They also said the improving sales trend seen in June and July, combined with adjustments in purchase levels, have helped realign inventories and sales for most broadline retailers so that second-quarter 1997 results will be better than expectations.

"We forecast that strong inventory and expense controls will lead to retailers' earnings outpacing the average earnings of the S&P 500 for the remainder of 1997," the analysts wrote in a news release. -- ((Reuters Chicago Newsdesk (312) 408-8787))
